title: American Express FY2022 Form 10-K — Table 4: Expenses Summary with year-over-year variances
key_points: Total expenses grew $7,985M, or 24%, in 2022 versus 2021, and $6,049M, or 22%, in 2021 versus 2020.

title: American Express FY2022 Form 10-K — MD&A commentary on expense drivers and operating expense efficiency
key_points: Management states that Card Member rewards, Card Member services and Business development expenses are generally correlated to volumes or variable based on usage, and increased year-over-year due to network volume growth and higher usage of travel-related benefits.
Management states it remains focused on driving marketing and operating expense efficiencies while continuing to invest in the growth strategy.
Total expenses increased in 2021 versus 2020 primarily driven by higher customer engagement and marketing expenses, reflecting higher billed business and increases in marketing investments.

Card Member rewards expense growth in 2022 was also driven by a larger proportion of spend in categories that earn incremental rewards such as travel and a higher mix of redemptions in travel-related categories.

title: American Express Company Form 10-K FY2022 — Business Environment & Executive Overview (billed business rebound, T&E mix shift, revenue lines)
key_points: Billed business rose 23% to $1,338.3bn in 2022 from $1,089.8bn in 2021, which was itself up 25% from $870.7bn in 2020.
Billed business represented 86% of total network volumes and is described by management as 'the most significant driver of our financial results.'
Worldwide network volumes increased 21% (24% FX-adjusted) to $1,552.8bn in 2022.
T&E-related billed business was 25% of total billed business in 2022 versus 19% in 2021; G&S-related fell to 75% from 81%.
T&E-related billed business grew 64% (67% FX-adjusted) in 2022, after growing 59% (58% FX-adjusted) in 2021.
Airline-related billed business grew 119% (125% FX-adjusted) in 2022 and represented 6% of billed business versus 3% in 2021.
Billed business growth 'began to moderate towards the end of the year as we lapped the steep phase of recovery.'
Management stated spending on the network reached record levels and credit metrics remain below pre-pandemic levels.
Management framed the year as demonstrating 'our growth strategy is working and our business is in an even stronger position today than before the pandemic.'

key_points: Total expenses were $41,095m in 2022, $33,110m in 2021 and $27,061m in 2020: +24% in 2022 versus +25% revenue growth; +22% in 2021 versus +17% revenue growth.

title: American Express Form 10-K FY2022 — Table 3: Provisions for Credit Losses Summary and reserve build/release commentary
key_points: Total provisions for credit losses swung from a net benefit of $(1,419)m in 2021 to an expense of $2,182m in 2022, a $3,601m unfavorable swing; 2020 was $4,730m.
Card Member loans provisions were $1,514m in 2022 versus $(1,155)m in 2021 and $3,453m in 2020.
Card Member receivables provisions were $627m in 2022 versus $(73)m in 2021 and $1,015m in 2020.
Card Member loans reserve build was $448m in 2022 versus a release of $(2,034)m in 2021; receivables reserve build was $165m versus a release of $(202)m.
MD&A states 2022 provisions reflected 'a reserve build of $617 million compared with a reserve release of $2.5 billion in the prior year.'
The 2022 reserve builds were 'primarily driven by an increase in loans and receivables outstanding and higher delinquencies.'

The 2021 reserve releases were driven by 'improved portfolio quality and macroeconomic forecasts,' in large part improved unemployment rate projections, partially offset by an increase in loans and receivables outstanding.
Card Member loans net write-off rate (principal, interest and fees) was 1.1% in 2022, 1.2% in 2021 and 2.9% in 2020; reserves as % of loans were 3.5%, 3.7% and 7.3% respectively.
Card Member loans grew 22% to $108.0bn in 2022 from $88.6bn in 2021; Card Member receivables grew 7% to $57.6bn from $53.6bn.
30+ days past due as a % of total Card Member loans rose to 1.0% in 2022 from 0.7% in 2021.

title: American Express Form 10-K FY2022 — Table 1: Summary of Financial Performance (pretax income decline, ROE, CET1) and Note 18 Amex Ventures
key_points: Pretax income was $9,585m in 2022 versus $10,689m in 2021 (−10%) and $4,296m in 2020, despite 25% revenue growth in 2022.
Net income was $7,514m in 2022 versus $8,060m in 2021 (−7%); diluted EPS was $9.85 versus $10.02.

Management attributes the net income decline to 'credit reserve builds and net losses in our Amex Ventures strategic investment portfolio in the current year compared with sizeable credit reserve releases and significant net gains in our Amex Ventures strategic investment portfolio in the prior year.'
Net unrealized and realized losses (gains) on Amex Ventures investments were $302m in 2022 versus $(767)m in 2021 and $(152)m in 2020, a swing of roughly $1.07bn embedded within Other expenses.
Return on average equity was 32.3% in 2022, 33.7% in 2021 and 14.2% in 2020.
The effective tax rate fell to 21.6% in 2022 from 24.6% in 2021, primarily reflecting discrete tax benefits related to resolution of prior-year tax items.
Common Equity Tier 1 was 10.3% in 2022 versus 10.5% in 2021 and 13.5% in 2020, within the stated 10–11% target range.

The company returned $4.9bn of capital to shareholders in 2022 through common share repurchases and dividends, and expects to raise the regular quarterly dividend by 15% beginning with the Q1 2023 declaration.

Management's forward-looking framing is qualitative: 'while we recognize the uncertainty of the geopolitical and macroeconomic environment, we remain focused on delivering sustainable and profitable growth.'

key_points: AMEX's 'Selected Metrics and Ratios' table lists network volumes, return on average equity, net interest income divided by average Card Member loans, net interest yield on average Card Member loans, effective tax rate and Common Equity Tier 1 — no operating margin, operating income or operating margin ratio appears.

AMEX's consolidated income statement presentation runs from total revenues net of interest expense to provisions for credit losses to expenses to pretax income; there is no 'income from operations' line item.

Segment reporting presents 'Pretax segment income' and 'Total expenses' per segment (e.g., USCS pretax segment income $5,400m in 2022 vs $5,958m in 2021; CS $2,880m vs $2,936m; ICS $578m vs $929m) without any segment operating margin.

By contrast, the Boeing FY2022 10-K in the same knowledge base reports 'Operating margins' of (5.3)%, (4.7)% and (22.0)% for 2022/2021/2020 and 'Core operating margins (non-GAAP)' of (7.0)%, (6.5)% and (24.3)%, with a full non-GAAP reconciliation table.
The presence of operating margin disclosure in the Boeing filing but not the AMEX filing indicates AMEX's omission is a presentation choice rather than a knowledge-base retrieval artifact.

title: American Express Company 2022 Form 10-K — Competition (AMEX competes as both issuer and network; peer set named)
key_points: AMEX states that as a card issuer it competes with financial institutions that issue general-purpose credit and debit cards.
AMEX states that its global card network competes with other card networks including China UnionPay, Visa, Mastercard, JCB, Discover and Diners Club International (owned by Discover).
AMEX states it is the fourth largest general-purpose card network globally based on purchase volume, behind China UnionPay, Visa and Mastercard.
AMEX states it faces intense competition in the premium space and for cobrand relationships from both card issuer and network competitors.
raw_excerpt: As a card issuer, we compete with financial institutions that issue general-purpose credit and debit cards. We also encounter competition from businesses that issue private label cards, operate mobile wallets or extend credit. We face intense competition in the premium space and for cobrand relationships, as both card issuer and network competitors have targeted high-spending customers and key business partners with attractive value propositions. ... Our global card network competes in the global payments industry with other card networks, including, among others, China UnionPay, Visa, Mastercard, JCB, Discover and Diners Club International (which is owned by Discover). We are the fourth largest general-purpose card network globally based on purchase volume, behind China UnionPay, Visa and Mastercard.

title: American Express Company 2022 Form 10-K — MD&A commentary on variable Card Member expenses and CET1 capital target
key_points: AMEX states that Card Member rewards, Card Member services and Business development expenses are generally correlated to volumes or variable based on usage, and increased year over year due to network volume growth and higher usage of travel-related benefits.
AMEX states Card Member rewards expense growth was also driven by a larger proportion of billed business in categories that earn incremental rewards such as travel.
AMEX states operating expenses increased 24 percent year over year, driven primarily by net losses on Amex Ventures equity investments versus prior-year net gains, and higher compensation costs.
AMEX returned $4.9 billion of capital to shareholders in 2022 while maintaining its CET1 ratio within a 10 to 11 percent target range.
